mainTopic: The reward for מצוות shown through a story about ציצית, plus rules for borrowed garments, מזוזה, תפילין, and how many commands one misses by skipping them
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier discussion: a slave is lower than a woman, so the ברכה for not being made a slave is still needed. A ברייתא then describes the חלזון, the rare sea creature whose blood dyes תכלת, and explains why it is so expensive. רבי נתן teaches that every מצוה, even a light one, brings reward in this world, with an unmeasured reward in עולם הבא. He proves it with a story: a man careful with ציצית was stopped from sin by his ציצית, and the woman later converted at רבי חייא's study hall and married him in a permitted way. Next, רב יהודה rules that a borrowed טלית is exempt from ציצית for thirty days, and a ברייתא shows the same thirty-day rule for מזוזה, except that a rented house in ארץ ישראל needs one right away. רב חסדא first limits the משנה's rule that the two תפילין do not hold each other back, but then takes the limit back, and the גמרא explains his first view as a precaution. רב ששת counts how many positive commands a person misses by skipping תפילין, ציצית, ברכת כהנים, and מזוזה. ריש לקיש begins to teach that putting on תפילין brings long life, and his פסוק comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A slave is lower than a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion: a slave is more lowly than a woman, so the ברכה of שלא עשני עבד is not covered by the ברכה of שלא עשני אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A slave] is more lowly.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words are the last part of an earlier discussion about the morning ברכות. The גמרא is saying that a slave is even lower than a woman, so a separate ברכה for not being a slave makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone suggested that the ברכה for not being a slave is not needed, because a woman and a slave have similar levels of obligation in מצוות. The answer is that a slave is lower still, so each ברכה has its own reason. This closes that topic, and a new topic starts in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave, the subject this phrase is describing

phrases.english: is more lowly.
phrases.notes: This ends a sentence from before: the slave is 'more lowly' than the woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from the earlier discussion about the ברכות of שלא עשני אשה and שלא עשני עבד.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A slave is lower than a woman, so each of the two ברכות is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A slave is lower than a woman, so the ברכה over not being a slave is not the same as the ברכה over not being a woman.

steps.title: What the חלזון is and why תכלת is expensive
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the חלזון: its body looks like the sea, its shape is like a fish, it comes up once in seventy years, and its blood dyes תכלת. Because it is so rare, it is expensive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: This חלזון has a body that resembles the sea and a form that resembles a fish. It comes up once in seventy years, and its blood is used to dye תכלת. That is why it is expensive.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ברייתא gives a short description of the חלזון, the creature whose blood is used to make the blue תכלת dye for ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the חלזון's features: its color is like the sea, it is shaped like a fish, and it rarely appears. The rarity explains the last line, that it is very costly. This helps explain why תכלת was hard to get and treated as precious.

keyTerms.meaning: The sea creature whose blood is used to make תכלת dye
The sky-blue dye used for one of the strings of ציצית
Its price is high, it is expensive

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source describing the חלזון. People who later tried to identify the source of תכלת have relied on it.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: This ḥilazon,
its body resembles the sea,
phrases.notes: This seems to mean its color looks like the sea.

phrases.english: and its form resembles a fish,
and it comes up once in seventy years,
and with its blood one dyes sky-blue,
therefore its price is high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about תכלת after the discussion of the ברכות ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חלזון looks like the sea, is shaped like a fish, comes up once in seventy years, and dyes תכלת with its blood. Its rarity makes it expensive.

steps.title: Every מצוה brings reward, even in this world
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן teaches that every מצוה in the Torah, even a light one, brings reward in this world, and the reward in עולם הבא is beyond measure. He points to ציצית as an example.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי נתן said: There is no מצוה in the Torah, however light, whose reward is not given in this world. As for עולם הבא, I do not know how much reward there is. Go and learn this from the מצוה of ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings רבי נתן's teaching about reward for מצוות. At the end he says 'go and learn from ציצית', which sets up the story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן makes two claims. First, even a small מצוה pays off in this world. Second, the reward in עולם הבא is so great that he cannot measure it. He links this to ציצית, which fits right after the discussion of תכלת.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'light' or minor מצוה, one that seems less important
Go and learn, a phrase that introduces an example or proof

steps.confusionAlert: רבי נתן is not saying a 'light' מצוה gets a small reward. He is saying that even the lightest מצוה gets reward in this world, and an unknown, huge reward in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Natan says:
There is no מצוה, however minor,
that is written in the Torah,
for which there is no reward given in this world,
and in the World-to-Come I do not know how much.
Go and learn from the מצוה of ritual fringes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן: אֵין לָךְ כׇּל מִצְוָה קַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the theme of ציצית and moves from the תכלת dye to the reward for keeping the מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every מצוה, even a light one, brings reward in this world, and an unknown, greater reward in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The story begins: a careful man goes to meet a זונה
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן begins his example. A man who was careful with ציצית sent four hundred gold coins to a famous זונה overseas, set a time to meet her, and when the time came he sat at her door.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story about a man who was careful with the מצוה of ציצית. He heard about a זונה in one of the cities overseas who charged four hundred gold coins. He sent her four hundred gold coins and set a time to meet. When his time came, he came and sat at her entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the start of the story that proves רבי נתן's point. The גמרא is setting the scene, and the story continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story first tells us the man was careful with ציצית. That detail matters, because the ציצית will play a role later in the story. The high price and the long trip show how strong his desire was, which makes the coming turn in the story more striking.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story, often brought as an example
The cities by the sea, meaning overseas cities

phrases.english: There was an incident involving a certain man
who was diligent about the מצוה of ritual fringes.
He heard that there was a prostitute in the cities overseas
who took four hundred gold coins as her payment.
He sent her four hundred gold coins
and fixed a time with her.
When his time came,
he came and sat at the entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה זָהִיר בְּמִצְוַת צִיצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the example that רבי נתן promised with the words 'go and learn from ציצית'.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's claim that a מצוה brings reward even in this world
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about a man who was careful with ציצית. This is only its opening, which sets the scene.

steps.title: He is let in and she prepares seven beds
steps.stepSummary: The maidservant tells the זונה that the man has arrived. She lets him in and sets up seven stacked beds, six of silver and one of gold, with silver ladders between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her maidservant came in and told her that the man who sent four hundred gold coins was sitting at the door. She said to let him in. She set up seven beds for him, six of silver and one of gold, with a silver ladder between each one, and the top bed was gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. The man is let in, and the woman prepares a very fancy, tempting setting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The details of silver and gold beds stacked high show how strong the temptation is and how far he has already gone. This builds the tension, so the next moment, when the ציצית stop him, will be even more powerful.

phrases.english: Her maidservant came in and said to her:
That man who sent you
four hundred gold coins
has come and is sitting at the door.
She said: Let him come in.
He came in, and she set up seven beds for him,
phrases.notes: The beds were stacked one above another with ladders in between, so the gold one was at the very top.

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁשׁ שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וְאַחַת שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: six of silver and one of gold,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת סוּלָּם שֶׁל כֶּסֶף,
phrases.english: and between each one there was a silver ladder,
and the top one was of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in Step 4, after he sat at her door.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's claim that even a light מצוה brings reward
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man careful with ציצית

steps.title: The ציצית slap him and he stops
steps.stepSummary: As he climbs up to sin, his four ציצית slap him in the face. He slides down to the ground, she follows, and she swears she won't let him go until he tells her what flaw he saw in her.
steps.simpleTranslation: She climbed up and sat undressed on the top bed, and he climbed up to sit undressed facing her. His four ציצית came and slapped him on the face. He slid down and sat on the ground, and she slid down and sat on the ground too. She said: I swear by the gappa of Rome that I won't let you go until you tell me what flaw you saw in me.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the turning point of the story: at the last moment, his ציצית stop him from sinning. She is confused and demands an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה he was careful with is the very thing that saves him. She assumes he stopped because something was wrong with her, which sets up his answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath by something important in Rome

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of the proof: ציצית, a 'light' מצוה, protected him from a serious sin, which shows that even a light מצוה has great power and reward.

phrases.aramaic: עָלְתָה וְיָשְׁבָה עַל גַּבֵּי עֶלְיוֹנָה כְּשֶׁהִיא עֲרוּמָּה,
phrases.english: She climbed up and sat on the top bed, undressed,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף הוּא עָלָה לֵישֵׁב עָרוֹם כְּנֶגְדָּהּ,
phrases.english: and he too climbed up to sit undressed facing her.
His four ritual fringes came
and slapped him on his face.

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁמַט וְיָשַׁב לוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע,
phrases.english: He slid down and sat on the ground,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף הִיא נִשְׁמְטָה וְיָשְׁבָה עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע.
phrases.english: and she also slid down and sat on the ground.
She said to him: I swear by the gappa of Rome,
phrases.notes: This is her way of swearing an oath, by something the Romans held important.

phrases.english: that I will not let you go

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתֹּאמַר לִי מָה מוּם רָאִיתָ בִּי.
phrases.english: until you tell me what flaw you saw in me.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאוּ אַרְבַּע צִיצִיּוֹתָיו וְטָפְחוּ לוֹ עַל פָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story from the setup to the climax: the ציצית stop him.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's claim that even a light מצוה brings reward
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ציצית physically stopping the man from sinning

steps.title: He explains: the ציצית were like four witnesses
steps.stepSummary: He swears she is the most beautiful woman he has seen, but explains that ציצית carries the words 'I am ה׳ your God' twice, meaning ה׳ punishes and rewards, and the four ציצית looked to him like four witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I swear by the Temple service that I have never seen a woman as beautiful as you. But ה׳ our God commanded us one מצוה called ציצית, and in it 'I am ה׳ your God' is written twice: I am the One who will punish, and I am the One who will give reward. Just now the ציצית looked to me like four witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: He answers her question. Nothing was wrong with her; it was the ציצית that reminded him of ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He explains the double phrase 'I am ה׳ your God' as two messages: ה׳ punishes sin, and ה׳ rewards good deeds. Seeing his four ציצית, he felt as if four witnesses were standing ready to testify against him.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath by the Temple service
To punish, to collect payment for sin

phrases.english: He said to her: I swear by the Temple service,
that I have never seen a woman as beautiful as you,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִצְוָה אַחַת צִיוָּנוּ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ
phrases.english: but there is one מצוה that the Lord our God commanded us,
and its name is tzitzit,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב בָּהּ: ״אֲנִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״ שְׁתֵּי פְעָמִים –
phrases.english: and it is written about it twice: "I am the Lord your God":
I am the One who will punish,
and I am the One who will pay reward.
Just now they looked to me like four witnesses.
phrases.notes: "They" means his four ציצית, one on each corner of his garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ: הָעֲבוֹדָה, שֶׁלֹּא רָאִיתִי אִשָּׁה יָפֶה כְּמוֹתֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question she asked in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's claim that even a light מצוה brings reward
steps.raayaSupportSource: The double 'I am ה׳ your God' in the ציצית passage, read as punishment and reward

steps.title: She asks for his name, city, teacher, and study hall
steps.stepSummary: She refuses to let him go until he tells her his name, his city, his teacher, and the study hall where he learns Torah. He writes it all down and gives it to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: I won't let you go until you tell me your name, the name of your city, the name of your teacher, and the name of the study hall where you learn Torah. He wrote it down and put it in her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is setting up its ending. She wants to know who he is and where he learns, which prepares for what she does next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her questions are no longer about herself; she now wants to know about his Torah world. This hints that she has been moved by what happened, and the story's ending will show the reward he receives.

keyTerms.meaning: Study hall where Torah is learned

phrases.english: She said to him: I will not let you go
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean the same thing.

phrases.english: until you tell me what your name is,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שֵׁם עִירְךָ, וּמָה שֵׁם רַבְּךָ,
phrases.english: and the name of your city, and the name of your teacher,
and the name of your study hall
where you learn Torah.
He wrote it down and put it in her hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ: אֵינִי מַנִּיחָתְךָ עַד שֶׁתֹּאמַר לִי מָה שִׁמְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing his answer, she asks who he is, setting up the end of the story.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's claim that even a light מצוה brings reward
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuing story, leading toward the reward he receives

steps.title: She divides up all her property
steps.stepSummary: The זונה splits her wealth into three parts: one-third to the government, one-third to the poor, and one-third she keeps. She also keeps the fancy beds.
steps.simpleTranslation: She got up and divided all her property. She gave one-third to the government, one-third to the poor, and took one-third with her, besides those beds.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The woman, moved by what the man told her, gives up her old life and splits her wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how deeply the man's words about ציצית affected her. She is leaving her old life behind. The beds are mentioned on purpose, because they come back at the end of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: beds, bedding (the silver and gold beds from earlier)

phrases.english: She arose and divided all of her property,
one-third to the government,
and one-third to the poor,
and one-third she took with her,
besides those beds.
phrases.notes: These are the six silver beds and one gold bed from step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After getting the man's details (step 8), she acts on what she learned and gives up her wealth.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's teaching that every מצוה has a reward even in this world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man saved by his ציצית, now showing the woman's change of heart.

steps.title: She asks רבי חייא to convert her, and he questions her motive
steps.stepSummary: She comes to רבי חייא's study hall and asks to become a גיורת. He asks whether she really wants to convert only because she has her eye on one of the students.
steps.simpleTranslation: She came to רבי חייא's study hall and said to him: רבי, give the order and have them make me a convert. He said to her: My daughter, maybe you have set your eyes on one of the students?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to רבי חייא's בית מדרש, the study hall the man had written down for her. רבי חייא checks whether her reason for converting is sincere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר needs to convert for the right reasons, not just to marry someone. So רבי חייא asks if she is converting only for one of the students. This sets up the next step, where she answers him.

phrases.aramaic: וּבָאת לְבֵית מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חִיָּיא.
phrases.english: And she came to the study hall of Rabbi Ḥiyya.
She said to him: My teacher, give the order about me
phrases.notes: She is asking him to tell his students to take care of her conversion.

phrases.english: and let them make me a convert.
He said to her: My daughter,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא עֵינַיִךְ נָתַתְּ בְּאֶחָד מִן הַתַּלְמִידִים.
phrases.english: perhaps you have set your eyes on one of the students?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָאת לְבֵית מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving away her wealth, she goes to the study hall written on the man's note.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's teaching about the reward of מצוות in this world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuing story of the man and the woman.

steps.title: She shows the note, and רבי חייא approves
steps.stepSummary: She hands רבי חייא the note the man wrote. He tells her to go and claim what she has 'bought.'
steps.simpleTranslation: She took the note out of her hand and gave it to him. He said to her: Go and take what you have acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: She answers רבי חייא's question by showing him the note. After seeing it, he lets her convert and marry the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The note shows her story is real and that she is not converting because of some passing crush. רבי חייא sees the whole background and tells her to go claim her 'purchase,' meaning the man.

phrases.english: She took the note out of her hand
and gave it to him.
He said to her: Go, take possession of your purchase.
phrases.notes: He means: go ahead and marry this man, he is yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: She answers רבי חייא's suspicion from step 10 by showing the note.
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's teaching about the reward of מצוות in this world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuing story of the man and the woman.

steps.title: The same beds, now permitted: the reward in this world
steps.stepSummary: The beds she once set up for sin she now sets up for him in a permitted way, as his wife. The story ends with the lesson: this is his reward in this world, and the reward in עולם הבא is beyond knowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those beds she had set up for him in a forbidden way, she now set up for him in a permitted way. This is the reward he received in this world, and as for the World-to-Come, I do not know how much it will be.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends, and the גמרא states its lesson. Because he kept the מצוה of ציצית, he received the very same thing he gave up, now in a permitted way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man held back from sin because of ציצית, and in the end he got the same woman and the same beds, but permitted. This proves רבי נתן's point that a מצוה brings reward even in עולם הזה. The reward in עולם הבא is so great that no one can measure it.
steps.whatToRemember: The man who kept ציצית and held back from sin later received the same woman and the same beds in a permitted way. This shows that a מצוה brings reward in this world, and an even greater, unmeasured reward in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Those beds that she had arranged for him in a forbidden way,
she now arranged for him in a permitted way.
This is the reward given to him in this world,
and in the World-to-Come, I do not know how much.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי חייא approves the marriage, the story closes with its lesson.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Keeping ציצית, even such a light מצוה, brought the man reward in this world, the same thing he gave up but now permitted, and an unmeasured reward in עולם הבא.

steps.title: A borrowed טלית: exempt for thirty days, then obligated
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a borrowed טלית does not need ציצית for the first thirty days. After that, it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: A borrowed garment is exempt from ציצית for all of the first thirty days. From then on, it is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא starts a new practical rule about ציצית. רב יהודה rules on a טלית that a person is using but does not own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a time limit for a borrowed garment. For the first thirty days it does not need ציצית. Once someone keeps it longer than that, it does need ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: the fringes tied on the corners of a garment

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule. It tells a person who borrows a four-cornered garment when he must put ציצית on it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says: A borrowed cloak,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם פְּטוּרָה מִן הַצִּיצִית,
phrases.english: for all of the first thirty days it is exempt from ritual fringes;
from then on, it is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends, the גמרא goes back to practical rules about ציצית with a new statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrowed טלית is exempt from ציצית for the first thirty days and obligated after that.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the 30-day grace period, using מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a guest in an inn in ארץ ישראל, or someone renting a house outside ארץ ישראל, is free from מזוזה for 30 days. Someone renting in ארץ ישראל must put one up right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: someone staying at an inn in ארץ ישראל, or renting a house outside ארץ ישראל, does not need a מזוזה for the first thirty days. After that, he needs one. But someone renting a house in ארץ ישראל puts up a מזוזה right away, because of the value of settling ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the 30-day idea from רב יהודה's ruling about a borrowed טלית. Here the same pattern is applied to מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier ruling, something temporary, like a borrowed טלית, gets 30 days before the obligation starts. The ברייתא shows the same 30-day pattern for a temporary home and מזוזה. It adds one exception: a rented house in ארץ ישראל needs a מזוזה immediately, because of יישוב ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The scroll put on a doorpost
Settling and building up the Land of Israel

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rented house in ארץ ישראל has a stronger מזוזה obligation by its nature. The 30-day grace period is simply taken away there, so that people will settle and stay in the land.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that someone renting outside ארץ ישראל has 30 days before he must put up a מזוזה, while in ארץ ישראל he must do it right away.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא:
One who stays in an inn in ארץ ישראל,
and one who rents a house outside ארץ ישראל –

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם פָּטוּר מִן הַמְּזוּזָה,
phrases.english: for all of the first thirty days he is exempt from מזוזה,
from then on he is obligated.
But one who rents a house in ארץ ישראל –
puts up a מזוזה immediately,
because of the settling of ארץ ישראל.
phrases.notes: Once the מזוזה is up, he is less likely to take it down and move out, so the people stay settled in the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's 30-day grace period with a parallel case from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The 30-day grace period for something used only temporarily.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about מזוזה in an inn or rented house.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits the rule that the two תפילין do not depend on each other
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the arm-תפילין and head-תפילין do not hold each other back. רב חסדא says this applies only when the person owns both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the arm-תפילין does not hold back the head-תפילין. רב חסדא said: they taught this only when he has both. But if he does not have the other one, its absence does hold him back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about תפילין. רב חסדא then narrows it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's simple meaning is that you can put on one תפילין even without the other. רב חסדא says this is only true when the other one exists but is not available right now. If he does not own the other one at all, he should not put on the one he has.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back; its absence stops the other from counting
They taught this only in a certain case (a limit on a rule)

phrases.english: The arm-תפילין does not hold back the head-תפילין.
רב חסדא said:
They taught this only when he has the other one,
but if he does not have it, it does hold him back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's rule about the two parts of תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two תפילין are independent only when he owns both. If he lacks one, he should not put on the other.

steps.title: רב חסדא takes back his limit
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רב חסדא whether he still holds his view. He says no: someone who cannot do two מצוות should still do the one he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Did you say that? He said to them: No. Rather, if someone does not have two מצוות, should he not do even one מצוה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא's students check whether he still holds his earlier view, and he takes it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His new reasoning is simple. Not being able to do one מצוה is no reason to skip the other. So a person who owns only one תפילין should put it on, which matches the plain meaning of the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The final view: if you have only one of the תפילין, you still put it on.

phrases.english: They said to him: Did you say that?
phrases.notes: His students are asking whether he still holds what he said.

phrases.english: He said to them: No,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַאן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ תְּרֵי מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: rather, one who does not have two מצוות,
should he not do even one מצוה?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אָמַרְתָּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב חסדא takes back his own limit from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole limit רב חסדא made in step 15.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Missing one מצוה is no reason to give up the other one you are able to do.

steps.title: What did רב חסדא hold at first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning was behind רב חסדא's first view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at first, what did he think?
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב חסדא's second answer seems so obvious, the גמרא asks why he ever held the first view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not challenging his final view. It wants to understand the logic behind the view he dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he think? What was his reasoning?

phrases.english: And at first, what did he think?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the view רב חסדא gave up in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רב חסדא's first view that a missing תפילין holds back the other.

steps.title: His first view was a precaution against laziness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that his first view was a rabbinic גזירה, so a person would not get lazy about getting the missing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a rabbinic decree, in case he becomes careless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רב חסדא's first view was a rabbinic precaution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was worried that if someone could wear just one תפילין, he would never bother getting the other. So he first said not to wear the one alone. The reason was to push the person to get both, not that the one would fail to count by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
In case he becomes careless or neglectful

phrases.english: It was a decree, in case he becomes careless.
phrases.notes: Careless here means not making the effort to get the תפילין he is missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His first view was a rabbinic safeguard, so the person would not neglect to get the missing תפילין.

steps.title: Not wearing תפילין breaks eight positive מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת teaches that anyone who does not put on תפילין fails to keep eight positive מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Anyone who does not put on תפילין breaks eight positive מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת makes a new statement about how serious it is to skip תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The arm-תפילין and head-תפילין are each commanded in four separate פסוקים. Each mention counts as its own מצות עשה. So 2 × 4 = 8.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the arm-תפילין and head-תפילין are counted as separate מצוות. This fits the conclusion that you put on one even if you do not have the other.

phrases.english: רב ששת said:
Anyone who does not put on תפילין
breaks eight positive מצוות.
phrases.notes: Head and arm, each commanded in four places: שמות 13:9, שמות 13:16, דברים 6:8, דברים 11:18.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין עוֹבֵר בִּשְׁמוֹנָה עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement about תפילין, related to the topic of the two parts as separate מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who does not wear תפילין fails to keep eight positive commandments.

steps.title: רב ששת continues: ציצית, ברכת כהנים, and מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת keeps counting. Without ציצית a person fails five positive מצוות. A כהן who does not go up to the דוכן fails three. Without a מזוזה a person fails two, because the Torah says וּכְתַבְתָּם twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who does not have ציצית on his garment fails to keep five positive מצוות. And any כהן who does not go up to the platform to bless fails to keep three positive מצוות. Anyone who has no מזוזה on his doorway fails to keep two positive מצוות, because it says 'And you shall write them' and again 'And you shall write them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting רב ששת from the last step. He gives three more examples of how many positive commands a person misses when he skips a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each number matches how many times the Torah gives that command. For מזוזה the גמרא shows its source: the word וּכְתַבְתָּם appears twice, so there are two commands. The point is that skipping one physical מצוה can mean missing several commands at once.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform where the כהנים stand to bless the people
'And you shall write them', the Torah's command behind מזוזה

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's full list: no תפילין means eight positive commands missed, no ציצית means five, a כהן who does not bless means three, and no מזוזה means two. Each number comes from how many times the Torah repeats that command.
steps.confusionAlert: For these three examples, the numbers do not mean these are different מצוות (unlike תפילין, where the arm and head are two separate מצוות). One act, such as hanging a מזוזה, fulfills several repeated Torah commands at once.

phrases.english: And anyone who does not have ציצית on his garment
fails to keep five positive commands.
And any כהן who does not go up to the platform
phrases.notes: Going up to the דוכן means going up to give ברכת כהנים, the priestly blessing.

phrases.english: fails to keep three positive commands.
Anyone who has no מזוזה on his doorway
fails to keep two positive commands,
'And you shall write them' and 'And you shall write them.'
phrases.notes: דברים 6:9 and דברים 11:20. The same words appear twice, so that counts as two commands.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ צִיצִית בְּבִגְדוֹ עוֹבֵר בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב ששת's statement from step 19, using the same counting pattern for other מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without ציצית a person misses five positive commands. A כהן who does not bless misses three. Without a מזוזה a person misses two, based on the double וּכְתַבְתָּם.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: putting on תפילין brings long life
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that anyone who puts on תפילין will have a long life. He starts to bring a פסוק as proof, and the פסוק itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: Anyone who puts on תפילין lives a long life, as it says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from ריש לקיש about the reward for תפילין. This line sets up the proof, and the פסוק will be quoted in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת described what a person loses by skipping תפילין. ריש לקיש turns to the positive side: what a person gains by putting them on, which is long life. The word שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר tells us a Torah source is about to be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is stated; introduces a פסוק as proof

steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the סוגיא from warning to encouragement. Keeping תפילין is not only about avoiding sin. It also brings a blessing of long life.

phrases.english: And ריש לקיש said:
Anyone who puts on תפילין lives a long life,
as it is stated:
phrases.notes: The פסוק he is quoting comes right after this, on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כׇּל הַמַּנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין מַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ששת's list of what a person misses without תפילין, ריש לקיש adds the reward for putting them on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever puts on תפילין is blessed with long life. A פסוק proving this is about to be quoted.
